questions.question: Classify solar, wind, coal, hydroelectric and nuclear power as renewable or non-renewable, and give the energy transfer for a wind turbine.
questions.expected_answer: Renewable: solar, wind, hydroelectric. Non-renewable: coal and nuclear (uranium). Wind turbine: kinetic energy of the wind → kinetic energy of the blades and generator → electrical energy.

questions.question: Explain how Koeberg generates electricity, starting from the uranium fuel.
questions.expected_answer: Uranium nuclei undergo fission in a chain reaction (controlled by control rods), releasing thermal energy that heats pressurised water; this heats a separate water supply into steam, which turns turbines connected to generators that produce electrical energy. Seawater condenses the steam. Nuclear → thermal → kinetic → electrical.

questions.question: Describe how radioactive waste from Koeberg is managed and why it must be isolated.
questions.expected_answer: Low- and intermediate-level waste is sealed in drums or concrete containers and buried in engineered trenches at Vaalputs in the Northern Cape; spent fuel is cooled in pools at Koeberg and later stored in sealed steel casks on site. It must be isolated because its radiation damages living cells and some of it remains dangerous for thousands of years.
